title: Freshness audit can overwrite JSON output with markdown
reasoning: When --output does not end in .json, `args.output.replace(/\.json$/i, '.md')` returns the same path. The script writes JSON to that path and then immediately writes markdown to the same path, destroying the JSON artifact. The CLI parser does not enforce a .json suffix.
reproduction: Run data-freshness-audit with `--output artifacts/data-freshness-audit`; the final file contains markdown instead of the JSON report.
recommendation: Either require --output to end in .json and fail otherwise, or derive the markdown path by appending `.md` when there is no .json suffix.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The CLI test only uses an output path named audit.json, so the markdown path differs and the overwrite path is never exercised.
suggestedRegressionTest: Run the CLI with an extensionless --output in a temp directory and assert the JSON file remains JSON and the markdown report is written to a distinct path.
minimumFixScope: scripts/data-freshness-audit.ts output path derivation and CLI tests.
